* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through late Saturday
night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST
Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and
other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor beach erosion
may damage coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal
water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying shoreline due
to sneaker waves. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off
of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which
may lead to serious injury or drowning.

the water, especially those who will be razor clamming. Keep
children and pets away from the surf zone. Keep off of
jetties, rocks and logs near the surf zone. If you see someone
swept into the sea do not swim in after them. Call 911 and
keep an eye on them until help arrives.

producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 6 at 3:18PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
A developing tropical disturbance, Invest 99W, is quickly approaching
the islands of the northern CNMI. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center
(JTWC) has issued a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert (TCFA) for 99W.
This means that development into a significant tropical cyclone is
likely within the next 24 hours. What this means for the northern
CNMI of Alamagan, Pagan and Agrihan is that you can expect an
increase in showers and thunderstorms with strong gusty winds as 99W
moves past. Invest 99W is currently not expected to move through the
northern CNMI stronger than a Tropical Depression. However, as with
all tropical cyclones, this could change.

Invest 99W is currently moving fairly quickly, which is a good thing
for the northern CNMI. At the current speed, 99W looks to pass
through the region near Alamagan Saturday morning or early afternoon,
not becoming a Tropical Storm until later in the day, west of the
islands. Invest 99W will be monitored over the next 24 hours for any
significant changes in expectations and the residents of the
northern CNMI should continue to monitor forecasts for any changes to
the current expectations. For now, prepare for increasing rainfall,
with isolated thunderstorms and strong gusty winds within the heavier
showers. Only 1 to 2 inches of rainfall is expected, with gusts up
to 40 mph possible.

For more information on Invest 99W, see bulletins issued by JTWC
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW and WTPN21 PGTW.
